value.content: Greater Arlington Beaches Citizens Planning Advisory Committee May 12, 2025, Meeting Summary Ed Austin Regional Park, PAL Building, 3450 Monument Road, Jacksonville, FL 32225 Meeting Attendance: CPAC Members: Amita Agnihotri, Osprey Point HOA; Larry Belge, River Woods – St. Johns Landing HOA; Cheryl Brantley, Hidden Hills Country Club Estates HOA; Pamela Brown, Osprey Point Homeowners Association; Michael Corcoran, Kensington HOA; Scott Cowitt, Hawkins Cove Owners Association, Inc.; Gary Dickinson, Grove Park HOA; Kacy Evans, Caroline Forest HOA; Delmas “Dedee” Harper, POISE, Inc.; Lad Hawkins, Communities of East Arlington; Tim Keeley, Chair, Kensington Association; Sheila Litwhiler, Beachwood Civic Association; Joanne McIntosh, Ashley Green HOA; Donnie Oulton, Glynlea Park Neighborhood Association; Eddi Parsons, Monument Oaks HOA; Jerry Petoskey, Old Mill Cove Community Organization; Nina Pougiouklidis, Ibis Point Owners Assoc.; Ramsey Salem, Queens Harbour POA; Wayne Van Doren, Old Mill Cove HOA; Debra Wagner, Ibis Point Owners Association Excused: Nell DeCoursey, Hickory Creek HOA; Lenore Hanapel, Covington Creek HOA; Alex Hoffman, The Woods Community Visitors: Chrissy Bott, San Jose Neighborhood; Herbert Ramsdell, Southside Estates Civic Association; Ed Radloff, Colony Cove; Fred Berley; Antonio Chang, Beachwood Civic Association; Jutin, Charter Point Staff: Robert Bautochka, Municipal Code Compliance; James Carroll, Public Works; Connor Corrigan, Planning & Development Department; Devan Holland, JPL; Joe Johnson, Executive Council Assistant, Council District 1; Susan Kelly, Planning and Development Department; Sharwonda Peek, DCPS; Lieutenant Benjamin Suydam, JSO; La’dora Taylor, Parks District Manager; Cheryl Riddick, JTA; Lieutenant Jarmar Smith, JFRD; Rosemary Wesolowski, Neighborhood Services Office Call to Order/Verify Quorum: Chair Keeley called the May 2025 GAB CPAC meeting to order at 6:30 pm. Rosemary Wesolowski verified that a quorum was present. Pledge of Allegiance Approval of the Previous Meeting Summary – Approval of the April 2025 meeting summary will be completed at the June 2025 CPAC meeting. Presentation(s): Susan Kelly, City Planner Supervisor, Planning and Development Department, City of Jacksonville, spoke on the City of Jacksonville Comprehensive Plan. The Comprehensive Plan is a policy document required by the Florida Statue (Chapter 163) and by Jacksonville’s Municipal Code of Ordinances (Chapter 650). The Comprehensive Plan lays out the goals that direct development of programs and policies that guide growth and development. The City of Jacksonville is currently using the 2045 Comprehensive Plan. The Comprehensive Plan consists of 11 elements, a section with definitions and a map series. The 11 elements are Capital Improvements, Conservation/Coastal Management, Future Land 1 | P age Use, Historic Preservation, Housing, Infrastructure, Intergovernmental Coordination, Property Rights, Public Schools’ Facilities, Recreation/Open Spaces and Transportation. Florida Statutes (Sec.163.3191(1)) require that local governments evaluate their Comprehensive Plans at least once every 7 years. The updates are subject to the public hearing process and must be adopted by the City Council. The City’s Comprehensive Plan in 2023 was updated from the 2030 Comprehensive Plan to the 2025 Comprehensive Plan. To view the 2045 Comprehensive Plan visit: Jacksonville.gov>City Departments>Planning>Community Planning Division>City’s Comprehensive Plan Susan Kelly – 904-255-7837 or Ksusan@coj.net Elected Officials Report: On behalf of The Honorable Ken Amaro, District 1, Joe Jackson, Executive Council Assistant, shared the following updates: • Phase 1 construction on the Lone Star Road extension is underway. This phase of the project is expected to be completed by fall 2025. Phase 2 of the project will improve the intersection of Lone Star Road and Mill Creek Road; a traffic signal will be added. • Regency Square Mall was sold, and Council Member Amaro has communicated with the new owners but has not received any redevelopment information yet. • On May 21, 2025, there will be a ribbon cutting ceremony for the new Blue Cypress Pool at 9:00 am at 5461 Golf Course Drive, 32277. • The next Council District 1 Town Hall meeting will be held on Monday, June 23, 2025 at 6:00 pm; the location will be announced in the near future. The Honorable Ken Amaro – 904-255-5201 Staff Reports: JSO – On behalf of Commander Alicea, Lieutenant Benjamin Suydam provided the following JSO report: • Shared the various crimes statics for each of the JSO subsectors that are in Zone 2. • The CPAC was reminded that spring break is around the corner, and everyone was encouraged to be mindful that there will be an increased number of kids out and about; be careful driving. • Everyone was reminded to participate in the 9:00 pm routine; remove all valuables from vehicles and lock your car every night at 9:00 pm. Commander Alicea – 904-630-8166 JFRD – Lieutenant Smith reminded the CPAC meeting attendees that Hurricane Season is upon us. Everyone was encouraged to download the JAX Ready app and to start purchasing items for their hurricane kits. As a follow up to a question last month. JFRD has identified the location for the new fire station in the Arlington area off Wompi Drive. Wompi Drive is off Merrill Road, east of I-295. A temporary trailer will be placed at the location for JFRD staff to work out of until the new fire station can be built. Lieutenant Smith – JarmarS@coj.net 2 | P age Jacksonville Public Library (JPL) – Devon Holland, provided the following information: • All libraries are preparing for the summer events. There are many fun activities planned that incorporate reading and learning so kids do not lose a lot of skills/knowledge over the summer. • On Saturday, May 31, 2025, at 10:30 am at the Pablo Creek Regional Library there will be a free genealogy class offered. Bring your library card to use a computer and guidance will be provided to search your family history using ancestry.com. • On Wednesday, May 21, 2025, starting at 5:00 pm there will be a photography workshop at the Pablo Creek Regional Library for free. • Please remember that JPL provides a lot of digital resources available for free that you can access from your home computer. One of the most popular free programs is Linked In Learning which offers unlimited access to over 16,000 courses on demand. Visit: https://jaxpubliclibrary.org/ • All the libraries will be closed on Monday, May 26, 2025, in honor of Memorial Day. Devon Holland – DHolland@coj.net JTA – Cheryl Riddick encouraged everyone to visit www.jtafla.com and click on the different tiles on the website to learn about all JTA’s programs and services that are available. As an update to the Automation and Innovation Center, there are 48 days remaining until the launch of Navi. The autonomous service has been branded Neighborhood Autonomous Vehicle Innovation or NAVI and is part of the Ultimate Urban Circulator (USC) project. The NAVI program will deploy 14 AV shuttles downtown by early summer. Cheryl Riddick, 904-630-3100 Military and Veterans Affairs – Fred Berley provided the following updates:’ • There will be a Memorial Day Ceremony on May 26, 2025, at the Jacksonville Veterans Memorial Wall, 1145 East Adams Street (adjacent to EverBank Stadium) starting at 8:00 am. • On June 2, 2025 the annual Spouse’s Night Out will begin at 5:00 pm at the VySytar Veteran’s Memorial Arena. No children allowed and no childcare provided. Please pre- register at tmorales@coj.net. Fred Berley – 904-255-5524 Municipal Code Compliance Division (MCCD) – Robert Bautochka shared the following updates: • In the past 30 days, 1,156 inspections were completed, and 84 snipe/litter signs were removed. • A special project was started today in the Atlantic Highlands community (off Atlantic Boulevard and Sunny Side Avenue).
